refuters.argument:
Verdict: faithful (not refuted). I searched for a concrete discrepancy, with the focus on the endpoint-join clause, and found none.

Definitions expanded to primitives: `Plane := ℝ × ℝ` (Polygon.lean:13, an abbrev, so `•` and `∑` are the ordinary Prod module/AddCommMonoid operations; no custom instances anywhere in Polygon/Chirotope/EuclideanPlane/DirectionProjection/TransportLengths). `planeDot u v := u.1*v.1 + u.2*v.2` (EuclideanPlane.lean:27) is the Euclidean inner product. `euclideanLength u := ‖planeComplex u‖ = Real.sqrt (u.1*u.1 + u.2*u.2)` (EuclideanPlane.lean:29-34) is the Euclidean norm, not the sup norm of ℝ×ℝ, so `euclideanLength (u i t) = 1` really says "unit vector".

Hypotheses, clause by clause. (1) "u_1(t),...,u_n(t) ... continuous unit vectors on a compact interval" (source lines 4) = `{ι} [Fintype ι] (hab : a ≤ b) (u : ι → ℝ → Plane) (hu : ∀ i, ContinuousOn (u i) (Icc a b)) (hunit : ∀ i, ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, euclideanLength (u i t) = 1)` (statement lines 19-21). ContinuousOn on Icc a b is continuity of the restriction; values of u outside Icc a b are never referenced in the conclusion (a, b ∈ Icc a b because a ≤ b). Arbitrary finite ι generalizes {1..n} (Lean stronger, meaning unchanged); the empty ι is not a vacuous loophole because hsemi is then false (v=(1,0) is a unit vector and `∀ i` over an empty type is trivially true), so the theorem places no spurious demand and admits no spurious instance. a = b gives the one-point interval, which the source proof explicitly admits ("For a one-point parameter interval the pointwise choice already suffices", sm-5-transport.tex line ~116). a > b (empty set) is not a "compact interval" with "either endpoint", so `hab` adds nothing beyond what the source presupposes. (2) "lying in no closed semicircle at any parameter" (line 5) = `hsemi : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ¬ ∃ v, euclideanLength v = 1 ∧ ∀ i, 0 ≤ planeDot v (u i t)` (lines 22-23). A closed semicircle is {w on the circle : ⟨v,w⟩ ≥ 0} for a unit v; the family lies in it iff ∀ i, ⟨v,u_i(t)⟩ ≥ 0. Exact match.

Conclusions. (3) "continuous strictly positive lengths l_i(t) with Σ l_i(t)u_i(t)=0" (lines 5-6) = `∃ l : ι → ℝ → ℝ, (∀ i, ContinuousOn (l i) (Icc a b)) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, 0 < l i t) ∧ (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ∑ i, l i t • u i t = 0)` (lines 24-27). Exact match.

(4) Focus clause: "At either endpoint, any prescribed positive closing lengths can be joined to the selected lengths while keeping the directions fixed" (lines 6-8). Decomposition: "at either endpoint" -> two clauses, one with `u i a, l i a` (lines 28-31) and one with `u i b, l i b` (lines 32-35). "any prescribed positive closing lengths" -> `∀ m : ι → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < m i) → ∑ i, m i • u i a = 0 →`; "closing" means Σ m_i u_i = 0 at that endpoint (the proof's own usage: "closing vector", "closure is linear"), and "positive" means strictly positive: the proof's last sentence says "the set of strictly positive closing lengths is convex. Straight segments in that set join any prescribed endpoint lengths to the selected ones", so the prescribed lengths are members of the strictly positive set. "can be joined to the selected lengths" -> for every s ∈ [0,1] the point (1-s)·m + s·l(a) is strictly positive and closes; that is exactly the straight segment from m (s=0) to l(a) (s=1) which the proof names as the join, and it is at least as strong as any weaker reading ("there exists a continuous path of positive closing lengths from m to l(a)") since the segment is such a path. "while keeping the directions fixed" -> the closing condition along the whole segment uses the constant directions `u i a` (resp. `u i b`), not `u i t`. The `l` in these clauses is the same `l` bound by the existential (they sit inside its scope), and the quantifier order ∃ l, ∀ m matches the source ("There are ... l_i(t) ... any prescribed ... can be joined to the selected lengths") and is the stronger of the two possible orders. I also considered the reading "l can be chosen with l(a) = m"; the source text "joined to the selected ones" and the proof's segment sentence rule that out, and in any case that would be a different lemma, not a sub-clause the Lean omits.

Weaker-than-source: none found. Stronger-than-source: the join is fixed to be the explicit straight segment rather than an unspecified path; ι is an arbitrary Fintype rather than {1..n}. Nothing printed lacks a Lean counterpart.
